race.name: The Divide
race.tagline: A steep, sandy northern-Michigan gravel race built around the Manistee forest roads.

adventure.explanation: Seasonal and forest roads around the Manistee National Forest, sandy sectors, and the rough Redneck Roughneck descent make the long route more adventurous than a standard county-road gravel loop.

altitude.explanation: Manton is a low-altitude race; the challenge comes from accumulated climbing and surface changes rather than thin air.

climate.explanation: Late July in northern Michigan can be warm and humid, but the organizer does not present climate as the race's defining hazard.

community.explanation: The Divide is part of the Michigan Gravel Race Series, supports Manton school athletics, and offers returning-rider and team discounts, giving the small event a real regional community role.

elevation.explanation: The organizer publishes more than 4,500 feet of climbing for the 52-mile long course, a high climbing density for a race of this length.

expenses.explanation: A small-town Michigan venue and unusually low entry fees keep the total weekend cost below most destination gravel races.

experience.explanation: Downtown Manton, national-forest roads, substantial climbing, sandy sectors, and named course features give the race a distinct northern-Michigan identity even without a destination-scale festival.

field_depth.explanation: Age groups and multiple equipment categories broaden participation, but the organizer publishes no evidence of a nationally deep elite field.

length.explanation: The long course is 52 miles, with 23- and roughly 32-mile alternatives for shorter categories.

logistics.explanation: The organizer gives a downtown start, packet-pickup window, start order, and pricing, but the final 2027 registration, route, aid, cutoff, and rider documents are not yet published.

prestige.explanation: The race has run since 2015 and belongs to the Michigan Gravel Race Series, but its reputation remains regional.

race_quality.explanation: Multiple distances, mass starts, age groups, timing, course marking, and more than a decade of production support a solid regional race, while the 2026 flood cancellation leaves the final return course unproven.

technicality.explanation: The organizer describes gravel, seasonal and forest roads, sandy spots, and a rougher downhill; skill and higher-volume tires matter even though the course is designed to remain rideable at speed.

value.explanation: Even the long-course entry combines a low base fee with a modest distance surcharge, delivering 52 timed miles and 4,500-plus feet of climbing for unusually little money.

cultural_impact.explanation: The Divide is a durable piece of Michigan's regional gravel calendar rather than a race with broader national influence.

course_description.character: A compact but climbing-dense long course on hilly gravel, seasonal roads, forest roads, and sandy northern-Michigan terrain.

suffering_zones.label: Outer Loop climbs
suffering_zones.description: The organizer places the largest hills on the Outer Loop used by the medium and long courses.

suffering_zones.label: Sandy forest roads
suffering_zones.description: Northern Michigan's sand base can interrupt momentum and punish poor line choice or overly narrow tires.

suffering_zones.label: Redneck Roughneck
suffering_zones.description: The named rougher downhill requires controlled braking and attention after repeated climbing.

course_description.signature_challenge: Manage more than 4,500 feet of climbing in 52 miles without losing speed or composure on sandy forest-road transitions.

logistics.overview: The organizer plans to return in 2027 after flooding forced cancellation of the 2026 race. The published annual rule places the return on Sunday, July 25, 2027; final 2027 registration and rider documents remain pending.
logistics.accommodation: Manton has limited lodging; Traverse City and Cadillac provide broader options.
logistics.getting_there: The race starts in downtown Manton, about 45 minutes by road from Traverse City.
logistics.parking: The organizer directs riders to Manton High School with overflow at the school's athletic complex.
logistics.spectator_info: The start and finish are at Railroad Park in downtown Manton.

climate.overview: Late-July northern Michigan weather can combine summer warmth, humidity, and changing conditions.
climate.wind_conditions: Forest cover limits sustained exposure, though open connectors can still be windy.

terrain.terrain_overview: The organizer describes gravel, seasonal, and forest roads with sandy spots and one rougher downhill.
terrain.key_features: 52 miles, more than 4,500 feet of climbing, the Outer Loop hills, sandy sectors, and the Redneck Roughneck descent.

history.overview: The Divide began in 2015 as a regional gravel race in Manton and became part of the Michigan Gravel Race Series. Historic flooding closed enough back roads to force cancellation in 2026, and the organizer announced a planned 2027 return.
history.notable_editions: The 2026 edition was cancelled because flood-damaged back roads remained closed.
history.growth_trajectory: The event remains a deliberately affordable regional race with three distances and multiple bike categories.

editions.note: Spring flooding left back roads closed

final_verdict.one_liner: A short, steep, sandy Michigan race that delivers exceptional local value.
final_verdict.best_for: Midwest riders who want a climbing-dense gravel race with forest-road texture and low entry cost.
final_verdict.not_ideal_for: Riders seeking a large national field, a destination festival, or a long-course route already finalized for 2027.
final_verdict.pro_tip: Train repeated short climbs and sand handling, then verify the repaired-road route before choosing tires or locking race-day pacing.
